appearance_facts.fact: Label: 'Solar output (MWh)'. Scale from 10,000 to 40,000 in increments of 5,000.
Label: 'Month'. Months shown: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May. Note: Months are not in chronological order.
The bar for May is the shortest, visually below the 10,000 MWh mark on the y-axis.
The bar for Apr is at approximately 30,000 MWh.
The bar for Jan is at 40,000 MWh, the highest value on the chart.
The bar for Mar is at approximately 27,000 MWh.
The bar for Feb is at approximately 20,000 MWh.

public_definitions: Review the monthly solar generation dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or escalated as a critical low-output anomaly for this reporting cycle.
Use the monthly solar generation dashboard as the evidence source for deciding the appropriate May low-output severity route for this reporting cycle.
May low-output route: Route May to standard low-output follow-up, Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review, Send May to background monthly record filing.
uncertain: The months on the x-axis are not in chronological order, which may affect interpretation of trends, but the task is to evaluate May's output relative to other months.
